dedupe_keys.name: jamaica nswma waste characterisation and per capita generation studies 2009 2013 2015

description: These three reports are Jamaica's national studies of what households throw away and how much, carried out by the National Solid Waste Management Authority. Survey teams sampled waste collected from selected communities and sorted it into categories such as compostable material, paper, plastics, glass, metals, textiles and electronic waste, then worked out generation per person. The 2013 report found that compostable material made up about 62% of waste collected and that per capita generation had fallen slightly in most surveyed communities since 2010, to around one kilogram a day or less. Reports for 2009, 2013 and 2015 are free to download as PDFs from the authority's research page. Caveats: the samples cover a limited set of communities, the 2015 file is a short scan without extractable text, the studies are now dated, and no licence is stated. Coverage is national in intent but based on community samples. Simulation uses: waste composition and generation inputs for landfill, composting and collection capacity planning in Jamaica, and estimating post-hurricane waste loads.
